name: TokenPilot

paper.title: TokenPilot: Cache-Efficient Context Management for LLM Agents

construction.unit: the agent's own message history, split into task segments; long tool outputs replaced by a preview with an archive key
construction.kept_as: messages verbatim; tool outputs over a size limit cut to first 600 + last 400 chars, full copy archived
construction.processing: rule passes at ingestion: volatile prompt fields → placeholders, tool definitions moved to the end, repeated reads deduplicated, long outputs truncated, HTML slimmed, images downsampled

organization.structure: active context (stable prefix + task segments) plus an on-disk archive keyed by content hash; a task registry labels segments
organization.stores: active context; artifact archive; task registry (active / completed / evictable)

management.operations: every B turns an LLM estimator updates task lifecycles; tasks marked evictable are archived and taken out of the context in one pass
management.forgetting: finished tasks the estimator deems no longer useful leave the context (code: replaced by a one-line stub; content kept in the archive)

retrieval.query: the agent's own recovery-tool call with an archive key
retrieval.candidates: exact lookup of the archived payload by dataKey
retrieval.selection: the agent decides when to recover; otherwise the whole kept context is read
retrieval.budget: tool outputs cut above 50k chars by default (30k shell, 20k grep, 10k mcp_auth, 100k glob/write/edit, read unlimited)

use.context: stable prefix + retained task segments with trimmed tool outputs (+ stubs for paged-out tasks)
use.reasoning: unchanged host agent loop (OpenClaw with GPT-5.4-mini in the experiments)

classify.note: The agent reads the whole kept context each call; the only lookup is the agent's own recovery-tool call by archive key, so 'read everything' fits better than 'agent searches'.

stages.ingestion: Before each model call, rule passes rewrite the prompt prefix (placeholders for agent id, working directory, timestamps; tool definitions moved to the end) and shrink tool results (deduplicate repeated reads, truncate long outputs to a 600+400-char preview, slim HTML, downsample images).
stages.construction: Trimmed outputs keep a preview and an archive key; the full payload is saved on disk under its content hash.
stages.organization: The context is a byte-stable prefix followed by turns grouped into task segments tracked in a registry with lifecycle states.
stages.update: Every B turns (B = 3) a Qwen3.5-35B-A3B estimator reads a compressed view of recent turns and the registry and moves tasks active → completed → evictable; evictable tasks are archived and removed in one pass.
stages.retrieval: No search: the agent reads the whole kept context. It can call a recovery tool with an archive key to get a trimmed payload back in full.
stages.answer: The host agent (OpenClaw, GPT-5.4-mini) answers from the managed context as usual.

summary: Context manager for tool-using agents that keeps the prompt prefix byte-stable for provider KV caching, trims tool outputs at ingestion with a recovery tool, and evicts whole finished tasks in batches when an LLM estimator judges them no longer useful.

headline: The aim is cost, not recall: keep the prompt prefix byte-identical so the provider's cache discounts it, and cut tokens only where that does not break the cache.
Nothing is searched; the agent reads its whole kept context and can fetch a trimmed payload back by key.
Whole tasks leave the context only after an LLM estimator marks them evictable, checked in batches of 3 turns.

discussion.takeaway: For API-served agents, cutting context text can cost more than it saves if it breaks the provider's prefix cache. TokenPilot keeps the prefix stable, trims tool output only at ingestion and evicts whole finished tasks in batches, lowering cost 56-87% at similar scores.

claims.claim: Lowest cost of 11 methods in every setting.
claims.evidence: PinchBench $3.22 isolated / $2.79 continuous; Claw-Eval $2.27 / $10.58, vs Vanilla $8.31 / $7.24 / $5.16 / $81.52. Tables 1-2
PinchBench 81.0 / 81.3 vs Vanilla 80.5 / 79.2; Claw-Eval 63.1 / 60.8 vs 64.5 / 63.4. Tables 1-2

claims.claim: Stable placeholders turn cold starts into cache hits.
claims.evidence: Cache hit rate 38.7% → 79.2% (PinchBench), 67.2% → 83.1% (Claw-Eval); cost $8.31 → $4.35. Fig. 4, Table 4
Without it score 80.9 → 77.1 and cost $2.87 → $4.03. Table 4, §4.4

claims.claim: Model-judged residual utility is the cheapest retention signal.
claims.evidence: $4.69 vs $5.17-$6.82 (category-grouped) and $5.25 vs $5.79-$7.04 (mixed streams), similar scores. Table 7

limits: The estimator can mislabel segments when interactions are ambiguous or sparse.
The frequency threshold τ and batch size B may need tuning per deployment.
Prefix stabilization helps only when the provider supports prefix caching.
Continuous mode groups same-category tasks; heterogeneous streams may reuse prefixes less.
reading: The contribution is a cost optimization for prefix-cached APIs; recall of past information is never tested apart from task scores.
On Claw-Eval TokenPilot scores below Vanilla in both modes (63.1 vs 64.5, 60.8 vs 63.4); the 'competitive' claim rests mostly on PinchBench.
In isolated mode the global layer alone (Table 4: 80.92, $2.87) is cheaper than the full system in Table 1 (81.0, $3.22), so eviction pays off only in continuous sessions.
The main continuous results group same-category tasks, which favours cross-task reuse; on shuffled streams (Table 9) TokenPilot scores 69.10 at $4.83, still the cheapest.
Savings depend on the price ratio: the cost model uses GPT-5.4-mini's 10× discount for cached input.
τ for the ingestion gate is never given, and the code's closest mechanism blocks repeated reads instead of restoring full content.
In code an evicted task leaves a one-line stub whose text names no archive key, so the agent has no stated way to recover it.

abstract.text: TokenPilot targets the cost of long agent sessions, where context grows with every tool call. The authors argue that pruning or summarizing history changes the prompt layout and so defeats the provider's prefix cache, which can erase the savings. TokenPilot instead fixes the prompt prefix byte for byte, trims noisy tool output before it enters the history (keeping a recoverable archive), and has a small LLM mark finished tasks for eviction only in periodic batches. On PinchBench and Claw-Eval it reports 56-87% lower cost than an unmanaged OpenClaw agent with similar task scores.
